elements.evidence: "Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience"
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One"
"Commerce One shall refund to Corio any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during committed term
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term"
notice is "thirty (30) days'" (better than fallback, but not the fallback figure)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: no early-termination fee imposed; condition absent

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination only at end of term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: Vendor barred entirely: "shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience"

reasons: The inserted 11.4 completes every atomic element of the preferred position: Customer-side convenience exit, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during the initial and renewal terms.

Fallback is not independently satisfied on its own terms (30 days rather than 60–90; Vendor given no end-of-term convenience right), but that is irrelevant because the locked preferred level is met and the deviations are more favourable to Customer.

Minimality is marginally exceeded by "in whole or in part", which introduces partial termination without any accompanying mechanic (scope, fee adjustment, or continuing obligations for the surviving portion); the preferred position requires only whole-agreement termination.

Untouched terms are preserved: the five-year term, auto-renewal, breach/insolvency termination, survival provisions and warranty-related material condition all remain effective, and no undefined term is introduced (Corio and Commerce One are defined parties).
The margin comment's fallback offer is non-operative and does not affect the operative outcome.
